messages:
alex: Quick Q — planning a small Terraform change to the GPU nodepool to add an annotation `redwood.io/pool-fallback=on-demand` plus capacity-reservation metadata so the autoscaler can route to on-demand when reserved capacity drops below a threshold. Want to make sure we don't regress preempt handling or taints. Thoughts?

mira: Can you paste the TF snippet you're thinking? Also does this require changes in autoscaler or our routing service?

alex: snippet:
```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "gpu_reserve" {
  # per-az reservation
}
resource "kubernetes_node_pool" "gpu" {
  metadata {
    annotations = {
      "redwood.io/pool-fallback" = "on-demand"
      "redwood.io/capacity-reservation-id" = aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.gpu_reserve.id
    }
  }
  # ...
}
```
This is mostly annotation-only. Autoscaler today reads `redwood.io/*` keys so should be straightforward.

rahul: Autoscaler currently checks `redwood.io/preemptible = "true"` and `redwood.io/fallback = "policy"`. We should update it to check `redwood.io/pool-fallback` too; small PR. Also confirm scale-down/eviction still respect taints.

jen: Related: do we need to adjust daemonset tolerations for gpu-runtime when nodes move to on-demand? Last time we used taints `reserved=true:NoSchedule`.

mira: We usually taint reserved nodes only. If fallback on-demand nodes are untainted they won’t get reserved-only pods — that’s intended. But for mixed workloads that can land anywhere, ensure podSpecs don't require the reserved toleration.

alex: Plan: reserved nodes get taint `reserved=true:NoSchedule` and annotation `redwood.io/reserved=true`. On-demand fallback nodes get no taint and annotation `redwood.io/pool-fallback=on-demand`. Reserved-only pods must have the toleration.

rahul: Also add a tfvar change: current var is `gpu_capacity_reservation_enabled`. Introduce `gpu_pool_fallback_policy` with values `none|on-demand|burst` default `none` so behavior is opt-in.

jen: Rollout suggestion: 1) apply TF change in staging, 2) update autoscaler to read the new annotation behind a `feature_fallback` flag, 3) create a canary reserved pool in a single AZ, 4) monitor pod placement and PDB disruptions.

alex: Canary SG/lifecycle snippet will be in the PR. Also question—secret wiring: we only add capacity reservation id as annotation (no secret), but EC2 reservation resource needs IAM. @mira can you confirm infra-account role has `ec2:CreateCapacityReservation`?

mira: Confirmed infra role has the permission. Note capacity reservations are AZ-scoped; TF should create them per-AZ (`for_each`) and tag them with `redwood:pool=gpu`.

deploy-bot: [deployment-check] terraform plan for branch feature/gpu-fallback: no drift, 2 resources to add.

rahul: Small nit — set `instance_type_map` to prefer `g5.2xlarge` for on-demand fallback so cost is predictable. Put mapping in `variables.tf`.

alex: OK will include that. Anyone object to merging later today if deploy-bot plan is clean?

jen: No objections from me. Add a short rollback note in the PR description for ops (how to revert TF and autoscaler flag).

mira: I'll review the TF snippet shortly. Also test in staging with `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` and `kubectl get pods -o wide` after apply.

alex: Thanks — pushing PR now. I'll ping here when plan passes. :rocket:
